cd /work; cat > transcribe.py <<'EOF'
import json, os, sys, time, urllib.request

BASE = "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2"
KEY = os.environ["ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY"]


def call(method, path, data=None, headers=None):
    h = {"authorization": KEY, **(headers or {})}
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, headers=h, method=method)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        return json.load(r)


def main(audio, out):
    with open(audio, "rb") as f:
        url = call("POST", "/upload", f.read(), {"content-type": "application/octet-stream"})["upload_url"]
    body = json.dumps({"audio_url": url, "language_code": "en_uk"}).encode()
    t = call("POST", "/transcript", body, {"content-type": "application/json"})
    while t["status"] not in ("completed", "error"):
        time.sleep(3)
        t = call("GET", "/transcript/" + t["id"])
    if t["status"] == "error":
        sys.exit("transcription failed: %s" % t.get("error"))
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"transcript_id": t["id"], "text": t["text"]}, f)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit("usage: run.sh <audio.wav> <out.json>")
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
EOF
cat > run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
exec python3 -I "$(dirname "$0")/transcribe.py" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x run.sh; ./run.sh sample.wav out.json; echo $?; cat out.json

The transcription step is built, and a run on `sample.wav` exited 0. It wrote `out.json` with a `transcript_id` and `text`. The text came back in British spelling: "organise", "colour", "centre" and "catalogued".

The step tells AssemblyAI to transcribe as British English (`language_code: "en_uk"`). The spelling comes from AssemblyAI itself, so I haven't added any post-processing to the text.

`run.sh` calls `transcribe.py`. The script uses only the Python standard library, so nothing needed installing. It uploads the audio, requests the transcript and polls until it finishes. If AssemblyAI reports an error, the script exits non-zero with the reason. It also exits non-zero if you pass the wrong number of arguments.

I left `out.json` from my test run in `/work`. It will be overwritten the next time you run the step.
